records.title: Scenario 3, Task 1: Develop a Simulated Investment Proposal
records.summary: Delivered a simulated US-stock investment proposal for a 25-year-old Hong Kong client with HKD 1,000,000, plus a plain-English client introduction. You confirmed the default assumptions (10+ year horizon, growth objective, medium-high risk tolerance, no leverage), so the plan is built on those. Allocation: VOO 45% (HKD 450,000), VTI 20% (200,000), QQQM 15% (150,000), IEFA 10% (100,000), cash 10% (100,000) — about 80% US equity, entered in three tranches (360k now, 270k month 3, 270k month 6). The proposal explains the reasoning (0.03% fees, a measured tech tilt, some non-US ballast, cash as a…
records.judge_notes: The team asked clarifying questions, received the client's default assumptions, and delivered a full proposal plus a plain-English introduction. The proposal covers allocation, reasoning, dollar-quantified risks, tax and estate-tax caveats, and an entry plan; the introduction is jargon-light and figure-checked against the proposal. Minor gaps (unverified 2026 YTD returns and 10-year Treasury yield, unverified withholding/estate-tax rates) are disclosed rather than hidden, which is acceptable for a simulated proposal.

records.title: Scenario 3, Task 2: The Future of the Semiconductor Industry: An HTML Slide Presentation
records.summary: Delivered a 10-slide HTML presentation, semiconductor_outlook_2026.html, for the fund team on the future of semiconductors from an end-2026 vantage point. It opens in any browser and advances with arrow keys, click, or F for fullscreen (also prints one slide per page). Structure: title; five executive judgments; the cycle in numbers (WSTS 2026F USD 1.51tn, +89.9%; memory +249.5% and ~53% of revenue); AI capex demand and the first digestion signal (MSFT/Google Q3-2026 capex below consensus, 29 Oct 2026); supply sold out through 2027 and the 2028 risk; China/geopolitics (bifurcated controls, ma…
records.judge_notes: The deck is a real, navigable HTML presentation with sourced judgments, investment implications and ranked risks, so the core deliverable exists. However, the valuation slide rests on forward P/E for only a few names with no consensus 2026/2027 EPS growth, and the market data uses the Spring 2026 WSTS forecast rather than the November update — both material gaps for a fund-team investment case, and the team itself flags the valuation section as not usable for a valuation conclusion.
